div.p: The development of software for Electric Load Management Center (ELMC) is presented in this paper. Based on the embedded real-time operating system VxWorks, ELMC performs multiple tasks including periodic and aperiodic ones. While rate monotonic (RM) algorithm is still used to process periodic tasks, we propose a condition triggered algorithm (CTA) to schedule aperiodic tasks by using VxWorks's semaphore mechanism. The schedulability test is also presented in this paper. We improved the test conditions to meet the needs of this system. At last, several tests are held and the results proved that compared with other scheduling procedures, the hybrid scheduling scheme has greatly improved the real-time capability and shortened response time for urgent tasks.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: Electric Load Management Center (ELMC) is a key component of the latest aircraft power distribution system [1]. An intelligent ELMC with high fault tolerance and reliability plays an increasingly important role in managing power supply of onboard equipment, and is critical to implementing aircraft missions. Here, we choose VxWorks as the operating system platform whereupon the ELMC software is developed [2].

In the evolution of ELMC software, a fundamental question is: how to design a suitable task scheduling algorithm to meet the requirements of the system. Two typical algorithms are hence developed: a static scheduling algorithm called Rate Monotonic (RM), and a dynamic scheduling algorithm named Earliest-deadline First (EDF) [3]. Although RM Scheduling has low CPU utilization, it is only applicable to periodic tasks; for EDF, however, it requires a large runtime overhead and has problem when handling tasks of the same priority. Therefore, a large number of improved algorithms derived from RM and EDF are proposed to solve specific tasks on different systems. Among them are three major scheduling methods that are able to solve both periodic and aperiodic tasks: background processing [4], server based [5][6] and slack based algorithms [7][8] [9]. Background processing and slack based scheduling use idle CPU time to deal with aperiodic tasks. The drawback of these two methods remains the lack of support to aperiodic tasks scheduling. Facing this, Reference [10] first converts aperiodic tasks to periodic ones, and by parameter estimation schedules the task set using RM algorithm. The main shortcoming of this algorithm is, it neglects the emergency requirement of the aperiodic tasks. In order to meet the specific real-time requirements of our system, based on RM, we proposed a condition triggered algorithm (CTA) that combines the VxWorks's semaphore mechanism to solve the aperiodic task scheduling problem.

The following sections are organized as follows: Section 2 describes the scheduling methods of ELMC software and analyzes the schedulability verification. The results from both simulation and a test under real-situation are presented in Section 3. Finally, Section 4 concludes the paper.

div.head: II. THE SCHEDULING METHODS OF ELMC SOFTWARE
A. Module partition
div.p: The central task of ELMC is to a) receive control information from the Power System Processor (PSP) through Airborne Data Bus, b) monitor and control the bus-bar of distributed power and Solid-State Power Controller (SSPC), then c) send the processed data to the PSP. According to ELMC's functions, the requirements on the software can be summarized as follows:
• To receive and process the control command through ARINC429 Bus, and the whole instruction cycle should be less than 50ms.
• The emergency orders must be completed in 2ms.

div.head: B. Task Creation and Priority Assignment
div.p: Prior to the task creation stage, the following rules need to be considered:
• To avoid code duplication and enhance software performance, each type of algorithm should be set as an independent task.
• Functions that are closely related should be integrated into one task, so the execution will be more efficient.
• When assign priority to tasks, it is necessary to consider the emergency requirements.
Based on the above rules, we establish six tasks-two aperiodic tasks that are assigned to the highest priority, together with four periodic tasks. Parameter specifications are shown in Table 1.

div.head: C. Task scheduling
div.p: For mixed task set, reference [10] treated aperiodic tasks for periodic ones with 1/λ as the average arrival time interval, and then use RM algorithm to schedule the whole task set. According to simulation test, we found that the algorithm's responses to aperiodic tasks are tardy. Considering the features of our system, we propose a new scheduling program: first, RM algorithm is employed to schedule periodic tasks; second, aperiodic tasks are assigned with the highest priority, and VxWorks' semaphore mechanism is used to trigger aperiodic task under certain condition. The scheduling of aperiodic task is shown in Figure 2. Suppose Task1 is a periodic task that may trigger two aperiodic tasks, i.e. Task2 and Task3, which have the highest priority. When the program is running, Task2 and Task3 are blocked by waiting for semaphore semId [1] and semId [2]. When Task1 arrives, if condition1 is satisfied, then "yes" is sent to semaphore semId [1] and Task2 will be performed; otherwise, if it fails to meet condition1 but condition2, then "yes" is sent to semaphore semId [2] and Task3 will be carried out. After the process finishes, Task2 and Task3 will be blocked again until required semaphore is available later.

div.p: Time demand analysis was first proposed by Lehozky and developed and perfected later by Tindell and others. The basic idea is to calculate the max response time of each periodic task and compared it with the time limit/deadline; only when the maximum response time of each the tasks is shorter than their respect time limit can the system be scheduled. div.head: A. Performance Comparison of Scheduling Algorithms
div.p: In the system, we use PowerPC8245 as the processor, whose highest frequency reaches 300MHz. With 256Kb RAM and 128kb NVRAM, this processor supports floating-point operations and memory management. The CPU uses ARINC429 to connect with PSP at a speed of 100kbit/s. In addition, the CPU uses 7 RS-422 interface to communicate with SSPC, at a speed of 115200b/s. Under such experimental condition, a comparison between the Scheduling Algorithm in our design (Algorithm 1) and the Scheduling Algorithm in [10] (Algorithm 2) is shown in Table 2. In Table 2, CPU utilization is calculated according to Formula (2), and the Real-time of the system means the time needed for a) PSP to send an order to the CPU, b) the CPU processes the order, and c) the CPU sends off the feedback.

div.p: According to the parameter specifications in Table 1, we can use equation (4) to calculate maximum response time max i t of each task, and compare it with the deadline of each task (Figure 3), and from equation (3) we could discern which task set is schedulable. The horizontal axis of Figure 3 represents the six tasks mentioned earlier in this article (see Table 1).

div.head: C. Results of software test
div.p: Figure 5 shows the scheduling results of the software after the test has been running for 6 hours. We conclude that the mixed task set is schedulable and each task meets their deadline; besides, the program stays stable after six hours' test. This paper presents the design and implementation of ELMC software based on VxWorks where a mixed task set was devised to cater to the requirement of the system. When scheduling the mixed task set, we propose a condition triggered algorithm: periodic task set are scheduled by RM algorithm, whereas for periodic task, we employed a hybrid scheduling scheme along with the semaphore mechanism introduced by VxWorks. This remarkably improved the real-time capability and CPU utilization; also, when compared with other hybrid scheduling schemes, it further cuts down the response time of urgent tasks. Meanwhile, this paper provides a new algorithm to facilitate the schedulability for mixed task set, and test results reveal that our software operates well in actual hardware environment.
